misconceptions.label: Choosing the hypotenuse from the angle θ, not from the right angle
misconceptions.description: The student picks as the hypotenuse a side that forms $\theta$ or faces $\theta$, instead of the side directly opposite the right angle, so the true hypotenuse ends up called adjacent or opposite.

misconceptions.label: Naming opposite and adjacent by where the side sits, not by the angle
misconceptions.description: The student decides which side is opposite and which is adjacent from its position on the page (for example the flat bottom side is always adjacent and the upright side always opposite) instead of from the angle $\theta$ being used.

misconceptions.label: Takes sine squared plus cosine squared to make 1 whatever the angles are
misconceptions.description: The student sees $\sin^{2}$ added to $\cos^{2}$ and accepts that the total is 1 without checking that the two terms are for the same angle, so they accept $\sin^{2}x+\cos^{2}y=1$ when $x$ and $y$ are different angles.

misconceptions.label: Shares the function out over the angle
misconceptions.description: The student treats cos like a number that can be shared out, so they accept cos(x+y) = cos x + cos y, or cos 2y = cos y + cos y, without working out both sides.

misconceptions.label: Uses a value from the other triangle
misconceptions.description: The student takes a number from the $30^{\circ}$ and $60^{\circ}$ triangle for a $45^{\circ}$ angle, or from the $45^{\circ}$ triangle for a $30^{\circ}$ or $60^{\circ}$ angle.

misconceptions.label: Gives r a minus sign
misconceptions.description: The student lets the position of the point decide the sign of r, writing r as negative when the point is left of the y-axis or below the x-axis, instead of keeping r positive.

misconceptions.label: Gives sec the value of cos
misconceptions.description: The student finds x over r correctly but writes it as sec, which is the value of cos, instead of turning the fraction over to get r over x.

misconceptions.label: Pairs cosec with cos and sec with sin
misconceptions.description: The student matches each reciprocal ratio to the ratio whose name it resembles, writing cosec as r over x and sec as r over y, instead of turning over the ratio it is the reciprocal of.
